sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Clicking the white block produced no change (board_changed is False). The underline is still under the purple swatch. Hmm.
Maybe the arrow keys move the selection frame, but the frame is stuck to the purple block, and the frame only moves when… no wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the arrow keys move the selection frame (the gray frame), and the frame is currently at the purple block's position. But pressing DOWN produced no change other than the HUD. Strange.
Maybe the arrow keys move the player, but the player is the frame and it can't move because… no, that's not it.
Alternative idea: maybe SPACE is needed to "activate" or grab the block. Or maybe the mouse click needs to be on the block, but clicking the white did nothing because white isn't selectable?
Let me try clicking the purple block, then clicking the white swatch in the top bar, and then pressing an arrow key.
Actually, let me think about this game from a different angle. The preview in the upper left shows the goal: white on top, purple on the bottom. In the main area, purple is on top and white is on the bottom. The swatches in the top bar: white and purple, with purple underlined.
Maybe this is a "color swap" game: click a swatch to select a color, then click a block to paint it that color? But clicking the white block did nothing.
Or maybe the arrow keys move the gray frame (cursor), and the frame moves one cell per press, but the frame is drawn around the purple block, and pressing DOWN should move the frame down by one row. But the diff showed no change in the frame. However… the diff only showed (63,63). So the frame didn't move.
Wait, maybe the arrow keys only move the frame when the frame is "free" (not overlapping a block)? The frame is currently overlapping the purple block. Hmm, that doesn't make sense either.
Let me try SPACE.
No, wait. Maybe the movement is applied to the block, but the block can't move because it's… no, that's not it. Let me try pressing UP and see if the purple moves up.
Actually, let me reconsider: maybe the arrow keys move the selected block, but the selection is purple, and pressing DOWN should move the purple down, but the white block is blocking it (collision). The purple is at rows 25–31, and the white is at rows 34–43. There's a gap at rows 32–33. If the purple moves down one row, it should go to rows 26–32, which doesn't collide with the white (row 34). So DOWN should have moved it. But it didn't.
Unless the arrow keys move the frame one cell at a time, and the frame is at rows 24–32 (surrounding the purple at rows 25–31). Moving down would make it rows 25–33. No change was observed.
Hmm, maybe the arrow keys do nothing until you click a block to select it, and clicking the white block did nothing because… the click was registered but the selection didn't change? board_changed is False.
Let me try clicking the purple block (row 28, column 31), then pressing an arrow key.
Or, maybe I should try SPACE first.
Let me batch the experiments: click purple, then UP, and check the diff.

sections.content: World model: Clicking the white block did nothing (board_changed False, underline still on purple). Arrow keys also did nothing to the blocks. Unclear what the interaction is. Next probe: click the purple block itself, then press UP to see if selection changes or the block moves.

<function=python>
<parameter=code>
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':28,'col':31}])
r1 = {k:last_action_result[k] for k in ('board_changed',)}
action(['UP'])
a = previous_frame.ascii.split('\n'); b = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
diffs = [(r,c,a[r][c],b[r][c]) for r in range(64) for c in range(64) if a[r][c]!=b[r][c]]
print("click_purple_changed", r1, "UP_diff", diffs[:40])
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['id'] in (7,8,11,12,13):
        print(n['id'], n['color'], "px", n['pixels'], "boundary", n['boundary'])
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
